q: At a booth in Tenali, a 17-year-old with Aadhaar demands vote saying he will turn 18 next month. Crowd pressures polling party. Your support?
options: Back RO: only 18 on qualifying date votes; record objection, no force voting
expl: Voting age is 18 on qualifying date.
why: Age cut-off protects roll purity. SI shields party from mob pressure and logs incident for RO report.

q: A constable-recruitment candidate submits EWS certificate showing flats and high income but presses for quota. Verification duty?
options: Verify 10% EWS quota criteria on income-asset norms; send fake to verification and fraud case
Reject all EWS claims as invalid
expl: EWS is 10% for unreserved poor on notified income-asset test.
why: Quota benefit needs proof, not assertion. Field verification stops creamy-layer fraud and protects genuine aspirants.
trapnote: Trap: treats EWS as caste certificate.

q: Women's group demands immediate one-third seats in today's panchayat draw, citing new women's reservation law. Your briefing?
options: Explain 106th law operates post-census plus delimitation; current draw follows existing reservation
Reserve seats by lottery on spot
expl: 106th reservation takes effect after census and delimitation exercise.
why: Post-census operation is built into the law. Premature enforcement would illegally unsettle notified rolls.

q: An MLA elected on Party A joins Party B for cash and still votes as A member while claiming split. Bandobast tense outside House. Legal position?
options: Defection is internal party matter with no law
Anti-defection disqualifies voluntary give-up or voting against whip subject to Speaker decision and judicial review
expl: Tenth Schedule penalises defection via Speaker adjudication.
why: Stability rule deters horse-trading. Police neutrality preserves House process while Speaker/court decides title.

q: Booth miscreants cite emergency-era powers to justify preventive lock-up of rivals without magistrate review. Your correction?
options: Preventive detention needs strict safeguards and advisory review; election rivalry needs BNSS bind-over/FIR, not political lock-up
expl: 44th curbs abuse: detention needs grounds, review, time limits.
why: Emergency excesses were later fenced by amendment. SI must use calibrated bind-over, not mass round-up.
